title: Testing a transplantation hypothesis in a Fabry disease model

sentences.text: This is a hypothesis, not a finding: its weakest link is the claim that haematopoietic stem cell transplantation targets lysosomal enzyme deficiency.
Test whether this approach can improve a lysosomal enzyme deficiency readout in a Fabry disease model, without proposing treatment of patients.
Before experiments, identify a suitable cell or animal model and assay; if unavailable, these would need to be built and validated.
Require an assay suitable for comparing the Fabry model with and without transplantation, preferably using the readout supporting the approach in its known disease.
Fabry disease involves deficient or absent alpha-galactosidase A activity.
Select a lysosomal enzyme deficiency readout that addresses this defect, and define rescue before testing.
Compare the same Fabry model with and without the transplantation intervention, using the same readout.

sections.heading: What result would change the plan

sentences.text: Rescue would support further cell or animal testing; no effect would retire this proposed link.
The shared mechanism spans multiple diseases and does not establish that Fabry disease responds.
The graph contains no study testing this therapy class in Fabry disease; support for enzyme supply by donor cells does not establish rescue here.
